## Goal
One pure-Python function that turns an article's Markus source into (a) validation errors an editor can act on, and (b) the `bodyIr` envelope stored on `Item`/`PublishedItem`. Every write path (CLI importer, publish step, editor Lambda) calls it, so `bodyIr` is always consistent with `bodyMarkus`. Also a small CLI so agents can validate a file without writing anything.

## Context (verified)
- Authoring format: `docs/markus-content-markup.md`. Papyrus markup (`::image{...}`, `[@key]`, `::citations{format=...}`) is NOT Markus: `src/papyrus_content/markus_renderer/content_markup.py` `prepare_page(text, images=ImagePipeline(), citations=CitationRendering())` lowers it to sentinel tokens `PAPYRUSMARKUP00001END` (`_TOKEN`), returning `PreparedPage` (`.markdown`, `.images: dict[token, ImageRequest]`, `.citation_keys: dict[token, list[str]]`, `.citation_lists: dict[token, fmt|None]`, `.entries` = front-matter `citations:` CSL-JSON). Markus never sees Papyrus markup (an unlowered `::image` fails with "Unknown directive 'image'").
- Markus: PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 (`MARKUS_REQUIRED_VERSION` in `markus_renderer/security.py`). `markus ast` implements `parse(text)`; `document.to_dict(markdown=make_markdown(allow_html=False))` (`markusmd.cli._cmd_ast`) returns `{ "type": "document", "schema_version": 1, "front_matter": {...}, "children": [...] }`. Verified: `printf -- '---
title: T
---

Hello **x**
' | markus ast -` shows `schema_version: 1`. TS mirror of that shape: `lib/markus-ir.ts` (`MARKUS_IR_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `parseMarkusDocument`) and `lib/markus-projection.ts`.
- Security invariant (`markus_renderer/security.py`): `--allow-html` is never used; `markus validate` is not an XSS control. Keep `allow_html=False` and keep the version assertion.
- Citation numbering/formatting: `markus_renderer/citations.py` `CitationRendering`, `CitationCollector.number_for(key)` (raises `CitationError` on unknown key when `strict=True`), `format_apa(entry)` / `CitationRendering().formatter("apa")`. Image src safety: `markus_renderer/images.py` `assert_safe_asset_src(src)` (rejects `javascript:`, `data:`, absolute paths, `..`).
- Front matter helpers: `content_markup.split_front_matter(text) -> (yaml, body)`, `read_citation_entries(text)`.

## Exact changes
1. New `src/papyrus_content/markus_renderer/derive.py`:
   ```python
   BODY_IR_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
   MAX_BODY_IR_BYTES = 300_000   # DynamoDB item limit is 400 KB; the item also carries bodyMarkus + metadata

   @dataclass(frozen=True)
   class BodyError:
       code: str          # "markus-syntax" | "markus-validation" | "image-src" | "image-attrs" | "citation-key" | "front-matter" | "too-large"
       message: str
       line: int | None = None

   @dataclass(frozen=True)
   class BodyDerivation:
       ok: bool
       body_ir: dict | None          # the envelope below, None when not ok
       errors: tuple[BodyError, ...]

   def compose_source(front_matter_yaml: str | None, body_markus: str) -> str:
       """'---
' + yaml.strip('
') + '
---
' + body when yaml is non-empty, else body. The body is VERBATIM (it keeps its own leading blank line), so import -> export reproduces the source file byte for byte when the file has canonical fences."""

   def derive_body(front_matter_yaml: str | None, body_markus: str) -> BodyDerivation: ...

   def plain_paragraphs(envelope: dict) -> list[str]:
       """Top-level paragraph blocks of envelope['document'] as plain text (inline text concatenated, soft breaks -> space); used by PPY-cddfb8's body[] conversion check."""
   ```
   `derive_body` steps: (1) `text = compose_source(...)`; YAML front matter must parse (`yaml.safe_load`, mapping or empty) else `front-matter`. (2) `prepare_page(text, images=ImagePipeline(), citations=CitationRendering())`; `ContentMarkupError` -> `image-attrs`; for each `ImageRequest` call `assert_safe_asset_src(request.src)` (`ImagePipelineError` -> `image-src`). (3) `import markusmd; assert markusmd.__version__ == MARKUS_REQUIRED_VERSION`; `doc = markusmd.parse(prepared.markdown)`; `ir = doc.to_dict(markdown=make_markdown(allow_html=False))`; `MarkusSyntaxError`/`MarkusValidationError` -> `markus-syntax`/`markus-validation` with `.line` if the exception exposes it. (4) citations: walk tokens in document order (regex `PAPYRUSMARKUP(\d{5})END` over the lowered markdown), for each key in `prepared.citation_keys[token]` call `CitationCollector(entries, CitationRendering()).number_for(key)`; `CitationError` -> `citation-key`. Build `bibliography` = `[CitationRendering().formatter("apa")(entries[key]) for key in first-citation order]`. (5) envelope below; `json.dumps(env, separators=(",", ":"))` longer than `MAX_BODY_IR_BYTES` -> `too-large` ("Article is too long to store; split it" with the byte count).
2. In-process Markus (no subprocess) so the same function runs inside a Lambda without the `markus` executable.
3. CLI `papyrus content markus-derive`: `--file path.md` (front matter + body in one file, `split_front_matter` splits it) or `--stdin`; prints JSON `{"ok": bool, "errors": [...], "bodyIrBytes": n}` (add `--emit-ir` to print the envelope). Exit 1 when not ok. Wire in `src/papyrus_content/cli.py`: add `"content:markus-derive"` to `PORTED_COMMANDS` (L204-231) and a branch in `dispatch()` (L379-393), plus a line in `print_usage()`. Implementation in `src/papyrus_content/markus_derive_commands.py`.
4. Export `derive_body` from `markus_renderer/__init__.py`.
5. Fixtures: `procedures/newsroom/tests/fixtures/markus-derive/` with `plain.md`, `image-and-citation.md` (one `::image{src="images/a.png" alt="A" layout="full"}`, two `[@a]` refs, one `[@b; @a]`, `::citations{format="apa"}`, front-matter `citations:` for a and b), `pull-quote.md` (`:::pull-quote{attribution="X"}`), `bad-directive.md` (`:::nope`), `bad-citation.md` (`[@missing]`), `bad-image.md` (`::image{src="javascript:alert(1)"}`).

## Data shapes (the `bodyIr` envelope; stored as AWSJSON string, compact JSON)
```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "markus": { "version": "0.5.1", "irSchemaVersion": 1 },
  "document": { "type": "document", "schema_version": 1, "front_matter": {}, "children": [] },
  "papyrus": {
    "images":       { "PAPYRUSMARKUP00001END": { "src": "images/a.png", "alt": "A", "layout": "full", "caption": null, "credit": null, "sizes": null, "loading": null } },
    "citations":    { "PAPYRUSMARKUP00002END": ["a"] },
    "citationLists":{ "PAPYRUSMARKUP00004END": "apa" },
    "entries":      { "a": { "type": "webpage", "title": "..." } },
    "bibliography": ["Formatted APA string for first-cited key", "..."]
  }
}
```
Sentinel tokens appear in `document` as ordinary text (a paragraph that is exactly a token for block images/citation lists; inline inside text for `[@key]`). `PPY-cddfb8` substitutes them (images -> assets, `[@key]` -> `[n]` numbered by first appearance, `::citations` -> the `bibliography` paragraphs).

## Tests
- Unit: `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_markus_derive.py` (unittest): plain -> ok, `document.children[0].type == "paragraph"`, `schema_version == 1`; image-and-citation -> 1 image token, `citations` numbering order a, b (first-reference order), `bibliography` length 2, `citationLists` has format `apa`; each bad fixture -> `ok False` with the expected `code` and no `body_ir`; size guard with a generated 2 MB body -> `too-large`; `plain_paragraphs` equals the source paragraphs for plain.md; `derive_body` does not shell out (patch `subprocess.run` to raise).
- Gherkin (behave): `features_backend/markus-derive.feature` + `features_backend/steps/markus_derive_steps.py`: Scenario "A valid article derives an IR envelope", Scenario "An unknown directive is reported with a code", Scenario "An unknown citation key is reported", Scenario "An unsafe image source is reported" (steps call `derive_body` on inline strings).
- CLI smoke: `poetry run papyrus content markus-derive --file procedures/newsroom/tests/fixtures/markus-derive/plain.md` exits 0; with `bad-directive.md` exits 1 and prints the error code.

## Acceptance checks
- `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_markus_derive -v` passes.
- `poetry run behave features_backend/markus-derive.feature` passes.
- Real content: `poetry run papyrus content markus-derive --file <a Pilobol.us article>` (clone `gh repo clone AnthusAI/Pilobol.us /tmp/pilobol-src`; files in `web/content/articles/*.md`) is ok for all 10 articles and `a-fungus-among-us.md`; print the largest `bodyIrBytes` in the ticket (if any exceeds 300000, raise it in a comment: that decides whether IR moves to an S3 attachment, a follow-up).
- Verify the TS side can ingest the envelope: `node -e` / tsx one-liner `parseMarkusDocument(envelope.document)` from `lib/markus-ir.ts` does not throw for every fixture.

## Dependencies
None (pure Python; parallel with `PPY-44a0f9`). Consumed by `PPY-b3a10e`, `PPY-22a3b4`, `PPY-3e5235`, `PPY-cddfb8`. The signatures above are a contract: dependents code against them, so do not change them after merge.

## Risks
- IR size: a long article's IR may exceed the 300 KB cap (the cap is why `too-large` exists). Measure on real content; escalate rather than raising the cap past ~350 KB.
- `markusmd` internals (`make_markdown`, `to_dict`) are not a documented API; pin to 0.5.1 and keep the call in one function so a Markus change is a one-place fix. The `markus` CLI behaviour is the reference (`markus ast`).
- Lambda cold start: importing `markusmd`, `citeproc`, Pillow (via `images`) costs time; do not import `ImageBuilder`/Pillow in this module (only `ImagePipeline` and `assert_safe_asset_src`; check Pillow is imported lazily in `images.py`, and fix the lazy import if not).

## Needs Ryan
Nothing.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-e169c5-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
